lines: TEMP=$(cfg temperature); TEMP=${TEMP:-0.6}
PARSER=$(cfg parser_name); PARSER=${PARSER:-json}
THINK=$(cfg enable_thinking); case "$THINK" in True|true) THINK=true ;; False|false) THINK=false ;; *) THINK= ;; esac
+TOP_P=$(cfg top_p); TOP_K=$(cfg top_k); MIN_P=$(cfg min_p); REP_PEN=$(cfg repetition_penalty)
# Lenient validation: an invalid value is logged and replaced by its default; it never fails the eval.
T0=$TEMP; TEMP=$($SYS_PY -c "import math,sys; v=float(sys.argv[1]); assert math.isfinite(v) and 0<=v<=1.2; print(v)" "$T0" 2>/dev/null) \
|| { echo "eval_config: temperature=$T0 invalid (0-1.2), using 0.6"; TEMP=0.6; }
case "$PARSER" in json|xml) ;; *) echo "eval_config: parser_name=$PARSER invalid, using json"; PARSER=json ;; esac
+# Optional sampling fields: unset (or a "disabled" value) means the server default; invalid means log and omit.
+if [ -n "$TOP_P" ]; then P0=$TOP_P; TOP_P=$($SYS_PY -c "import math,sys; v=float(sys.argv[1]); assert math.isfinite(v) and 0<v<=1; print(v)" "$P0" 2>/dev/null) \
+  || { echo "eval_config: top_p=$P0 invalid (0-1], omitting"; TOP_P=; }; fi
+if [ -n "$TOP_K" ]; then K0=$TOP_K; TOP_K=$($SYS_PY -c "import sys; v=float(sys.argv[1]); assert v==int(v) and (v>=1 or v in (0,-1)); print('' if v in (0,-1) else int(v))" "$K0" 2>/dev/null) \
+  || { echo "eval_config: top_k=$K0 invalid, omitting"; TOP_K=; }; fi
+if [ -n "$MIN_P" ]; then M0=$MIN_P; MIN_P=$($SYS_PY -c "import math,sys; v=float(sys.argv[1]); assert math.isfinite(v) and 0<=v<=1; print(v)" "$M0" 2>/dev/null) \
+  || { echo "eval_config: min_p=$M0 invalid (0-1], omitting"; MIN_P=; }; fi
+if [ -n "$REP_PEN" ]; then R0=$REP_PEN; REP_PEN=$($SYS_PY -c "import math,sys; v=float(sys.argv[1]); assert math.isfinite(v) and 0<v<=2; print(v)" "$R0" 2>/dev/null) \
+  || { echo "eval_config: repetition_penalty=$R0 invalid (0-2], omitting"; REP_PEN=; }; fi
+# Serving budgets. The server window is shared: input + output <= CTX on every request, and SGLang rejects
+# (input + max_new_tokens) > CTX. MAX_OUT must therefore be reserved out of CTX, not added to it.
+# Harbor decides when to summarize/unwind from litellm's token_counter, which for an unknown hosted_vllm model
+# counts with OpenAI cl100k, not the Qwen tokenizer. On terminal/code text cl100k undercounts Qwen tokens
+# (measured counted/actual 0.73-0.91 on this box), so max_input_tokens (Harbor's limit, in counted tokens) is
+# budgeted at 75% of the true usable input: (65536-8192)*0.75 = 43008. At that budget even Harbor's fallback
+# unwind (free counted tokens >= 4000) plus the summary prompt and an 8192-token reply fit the real window.
+MAX_INPUT_COUNTED=43008
+# Per-call sampling for every model turn (agent and summarization subagents alike). model_info alone does NOT
+# cap output: Harbor's LiteLLM chat path never turns max_output_tokens into a request limit, so max_tokens must
+# be sent explicitly. top_k/min_p/repetition_penalty are not LiteLLM OpenAI params for hosted_vllm (they would
+# be dropped), so they travel in extra_body, which LiteLLM merges into the SGLang request body.
+LLM_KWARGS=$($SYS_PY -c "
+import json,sys
+top_p,top_k,min_p,rep_pen,max_out = sys.argv[1:6]
+kw = {'max_tokens': int(max_out)}
+if top_p: kw['top_p'] = float(top_p)
+extra = {}
+if top_k: extra['top_k'] = int(top_k)
+if min_p: extra['min_p'] = float(min_p)
+if rep_pen: extra['repetition_penalty'] = float(rep_pen)
+if extra: kw['extra_body'] = extra
+print(json.dumps(kw, separators=(',', ':')))" "$TOP_P" "$TOP_K" "$MIN_P" "$REP_PEN" "$MAX_OUT")
# Model dir: the checkpoint's hf_config + weights, but always the BASE chat template.
M=/tmp/eval_model; rm -rf "$M"; mkdir -p "$M"
